title: J&K to witness widespread rains, snowfall on Nov 12-13 - The Kashmir Images Newspaper
full_text:
Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir is likely to witness fresh spells of rain and snowfall from November 10 onwards as a relatively intense Western Disturbance is expected to bring widespread precipitation across the Union Territory on November 12 and 13.
Director of the Meteorological Centre Srinagar, Dr Mukhtar Ahmad, said an initial Western Disturbance would approach Jammu and Kashmir on November 10, bringing a possibility of light snowfall over isolated mountainous areas, particularly in North and Central Kashmir.
He said another Western Disturbance of moderate intensity is expected to affect the region around November 12, with the possibility of widespread snowfall across the higher reaches of North, Central and South Kashmir, as well as the Pir Panjal and Chenab Valley regions.
Some higher-altitude areas could receive moderate snowfall, while thunderstorms and gusty winds are also possible during the period, Ahmad said.
He cautioned that fresh snowfall could disrupt traffic on important mountain passes and hilly roads, including Zojila, Sadhna Pass, Razdan Pass, Mughal Road and Sinthan Top.
Travellers, tourists, transporters and the general public have been advised to plan their journeys accordingly, check road and highway conditions before setting out and follow traffic advisories issued by the authorities.
The MeT Centre has also advised farmers to suspend harvesting activities during November 12 and 13 and ensure safe storage of crops that have already been harvested.
The Director MeT said temperatures could witness a significant decline following the precipitation, with daytime temperatures remaining around 5-8 degrees below normal during the subsequent period.
Meanwhile, weather conditions remained dry across Jammu and Kashmir on Monday, with the Meteorological Centre recording no rainfall during the preceding 24 hours.
According to the department’s station-wise data, Shopian recorded a minimum temperature of minus 0.7 degrees Celsius, while Pulwama recorded minus 0.1 degrees Celsius. Srinagar recorded a minimum of 1 degree Celsius at the automatic weather station in the city.

title: PIB Clears Rs 1,400-Crore Grant For Sawalkote Project, Refers Rs 18,730-Crore Debt Proposal For Separate Review - Kashmir Life
full_text:
SRINAGAR: The Public Investment Board (PIB) has approved a Rs 1,400-crore grant for infrastructure development at Jammu and Kashmir’s 1,800-MW Sawalkote hydropower project on the Chenab river, while referring a separate proposal for Rs 18,730.25 crore in subordinate debt to the Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs for consideration.
According to official records accessed by ETV Bharat, the PIB has cleared the project’s funding structure with a debt-equity ratio of 75:25. However, it has not approved the proposed subordinate debt support sought by the Union Ministry of Power.
The Power Ministry had proposed interest-free subordinate debt of Rs 18,730.25 crore during the construction period, to be repaid at an interest rate of one per cent annually over 25 years after the project begins commercial operations.
The proposed financial support was intended to reduce the project’s power tariff from more than Rs 9.57 per unit to above Rs 5 per unit, thereby improving its commercial viability.
The total project cost has been revised to Rs 26,373 crore from the earlier estimate of Rs 35,000 crore. NHPC’s 25 per cent equity contribution has been fixed at Rs 6,243 crore.
Conditions Attached To Approval
The PIB has stipulated that any increase in the equity cost will have to be borne by NHPC, the project’s executing agency. It has also set August 2036 as the tentative completion deadline.
The board has further asked the Power Ministry to include a comparative assessment of costs incurred on NHPC’s other hydropower projects in the draft proposal to be placed before the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
The project still requires formal CCEA approval before construction can formally begin.
Jammu and Kashmir was represented at the PIB meeting by Jammu and Kashmir State Power Development Corporation (JKSPDC) Managing Director Rahul Yadav, who supported the project.
Yadav sought an assurance that the project would be handed back to the Union Territory government free of all encumbrances after 40 years of commercial operations.
He also raised concerns over the reduction in the project’s design energy from 7,994 million units to 7,010 million units, arguing that the revision would reduce the region’s free-power share. He sought compensation for the anticipated loss, but the PIB did not address the issue in its recommendations.
Four-Decade-Old Project
Sawalkote is Jammu and Kashmir’s largest hydropower project, with a proposed installed capacity of 1,800 MW. Spread across three districts, including Ramban in the Jammu region, it covers more than 1,401 hectares, of which over 840 hectares comprise forest land.
Originally developed by JKSPDC, the project remained stalled for nearly four decades amid administrative hurdles, environmental concerns and objections from Pakistan over the construction of a dam on the Chenab river.
The project gained fresh momentum after the Union Territory administration handed it over to NHPC in 2021 under a build-own-operate-transfer model for 40 years.
Its revival has also coincided with India’s suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025.
Disagreement Over Project Control
The project has also brought into focus differences over the control of power-sector institutions in Jammu and Kashmir.
Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, who also holds the Power portfolio, told ETV Bharat that the elected government had limited control over JKSPDC and its decisions.
“Unfortunately, the elected government has no control over the JKPDC or its decisions,” Abdullah said when asked whether the Jammu and Kashmir government intended to develop the project independently or through a joint venture with NHPC.
The corporation’s board is headed by Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha.
Meanwhile, NHPC opened the first bid worth Rs 5,129 crore in September for Lot 1 Package, covering civil and hydro-mechanical works.
Major infrastructure companies, including Adani Group, Hindustan Construction Company, Patel Engineering, Larsen & Toubro and Rithwik Projects, are among those competing for the contract.
